title: Control plane versus data plane (who configures vs who serves traffic)
hook: The control plane is where you create and configure resources. The data plane is where your users' requests actually flow. Confusing the two leads to wrong answers about outages, permissions, and blast radius.

blocks.text: Every AWS service has a control plane API for management operations (create VPC, attach policy, update Auto Scaling group) and a data plane for workload traffic (HTTP requests through Application Load Balancer, object GET/PUT to Simple Storage Service (S3), SQL queries to Relational Database Service (RDS)). Control plane calls use IAM credentials and often hit regional endpoints like ec2.amazonaws.com. Data plane endpoints serve application traffic at high scale.

entries.plainDefinition: APIs that create, update, delete, and describe resources.
entries.example: aws ec2 run-instances is a control plane call.

entries.plainDefinition: Where customer workload traffic is processed.
entries.example: A user downloading a file from S3 hits the data plane.

entries.plainDefinition: DNS name scoped to a Region for API calls.
entries.example: s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com for data plane in us-east-1.

blocks.text: Outages are often plane-specific: S3 data plane may be healthy while the console (control plane) is degraded. IAM policies can allow data plane access (s3:GetObject) while denying control plane (s3:CreateBucket). Service Control Policies (SCPs) and permission boundaries frequently target control plane actions to prevent infrastructure tampering while allowing application traffic.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: control plane configures; data plane serves. Different endpoints, different IAM actions, different failure modes.

items.title: Control plane: create ALB
items.body: elasticloadbalancing API registers listeners and target groups.

items.title: Control plane: register targets
items.body: EC2 instances join the target group via API.

items.title: Data plane: user HTTP GET
items.body: Traffic flows through ALB to healthy targets — no run-instances call involved.

items.title: Observability split
items.body: CloudTrail logs control plane; access logs and metrics cover data plane.

diagram.title: Control vs data plane
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  Admin[IAM principal] -->|control plane API| CP[AWS management APIs]
  CP -->|creates| RES[ALB / EC2 / S3 bucket]
  User[End user] -->|data plane traffic| DP[ALB / S3 / RDS]
  RES --> DP

snippet.label: CLI: control plane vs data plane actions
snippet.code:
# Control plane — creates infrastructure
aws elbv2 create-load-balancer \
  --name app-alb --subnets subnet-a subnet-b --scheme internet-facing

# Data plane — application traffic (curl hits ALB DNS, not this CLI)
curl -s https://app-alb-123456789.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com/health
snippet.explanation: create-load-balancer is management API. curl exercises the data plane listener your users hit.

snippet.label: CloudFormation: ALB control plane resource
snippet.code:
Resources:
  AppLoadBalancer:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
    Properties:
      Scheme: internet-facing
      Subnets:
        - !Ref PublicSubnetA
        - !Ref PublicSubnetB
  Listener:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::Listener
    Properties:
      LoadBalancerArn: !Ref AppLoadBalancer
      Port: 443
      Protocol: HTTPS
snippet.explanation: CloudFormation drives the control plane to declare listeners. User HTTPS traffic is data plane once deployed.

snippet.label: CLI: IAM policy scoped to data plane only
snippet.explanation: Grant s3:GetObject/PutObject (data plane) without s3:DeleteBucket (control plane). Split permissions by plane in production roles.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Granting s3:* when the app only needs GetObject. Assuming a console outage means your API is down. Forgetting CloudTrail only captures control plane API calls, not S3 object access (use S3 server access logging).

interviewTakeaways: Control plane APIs manage resources; data plane handles customer workload traffic.
IAM policies should separate management actions from data access — least privilege per plane.
Use CloudTrail for control plane audit; use service-specific logs for data plane.
60s: Configure via control plane, serve via data plane. Different endpoints, IAM actions, and outage profiles. s3:CreateBucket vs s3:GetObject is the classic split.
Follow-up: how do VPC endpoints affect control plane versus data plane traffic?
commonPitfalls: Saying CloudTrail logs all S3 access — saying that gets you rejected because object GET/PUT needs S3 access logging or CloudTrail data events.
Strong answer: CloudTrail management events for control plane; enable data events or access logs for object-level audit.
Giving application roles ec2:* instead of only what deployment needs.
Diagnosing user-facing outage by checking only the AWS Health Dashboard control plane status.

jsTsCorrelations.note: SDK calls like s3.send(new PutObjectCommand()) hit the S3 data plane API. CloudFormation deploys via control plane. Your Express app serving users is yet another data plane unless it only calls AWS APIs.
